text:
alex wang: FYI: Customer on-prem tenant started seeing intermittent mTLS handshake failures to the private control plane after they flipped a new egress appliance yesterday. Errors show 'handshake failure' in our control-plane LB logs. Repro steps: from their side `curl --cert client.pem --key client.key https://controlplane.private.redwood.internal:443` sometimes times out or returns 400. Any quick checks? :eyes:

maria rodriguez: Can you paste the LB error lines and a tcpdump from their egress? Also which cluster/region?

alex wang: cluster: us-west-2-private-01
LB logs:
```
2026-01-22T09:12:13Z lb-01 ERROR tls_handshake: alert(40) from 10.10.5.23: peer closed connection during handshake
```
Attached tcpdump snippet from customer's egress (trimmed):
```
14:12:13.123456 IP 198.51.100.12.53210 > 192.0.2.45.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:1313, ack 1, win 229, length 1312
14:12:13.123457 IP 198.51.100.12.53210 > 192.0.2.45.443: Flags [P.], seq 1313:2625, ack 1, win 229, length 1312
14:12:13.123458 IP 198.51.100.12.53210 > 192.0.2.45.443: Flags [F.], seq 2625:2665, ack 1, length 40
```
Looks like ClientHello is being fragmented/truncated on the wire.

cheng li: That pattern smells like MSS/MTU or an inline TLS proxy rewriting/terminating chunks. Do they have a NGFW or TLS inspection device in front of egress? Also ask them to capture the first ~1KB on the server-side rx to confirm ClientHello bytes.

alex wang: They confirmed a new Palo Alto NGFW was put inline. Customer ran `openssl s_client -connect controlplane.private.redwood.internal:443 -cert client.pem -key client.key -msg -state` and saw repeated 'SSL alert number 40' and no CertificateVerify from server side.

maria rodriguez: Two quick reproductions to try:
1) From a host behind same egress, `tcpdump -s 0 -w clienthello.pcap port 443` and share the pcap.
2) Ask customer to add `controlplane.private.redwood.internal` to TLS-bypass / allowlist on the NGFW. If bypass fixes it, it's inspection/fragmentation.

networking-team-bot: Note: customer tenant t-9823 temporarily routed control-plane traffic via their non-inspected route for testing (route table change).

alex wang: We had them add TLS-bypass for the control plane. After the bypass, handshake stabilized — no more alert(40) in LB logs and connections complete normally. Customer will engage NGFW vendor.

cheng li: For long-term guidance: NGFW should not drop or mishandle fragmented ClientHello. Options for them: enable TLS bypass for this destination, enable MSS clamping on the NGFW to avoid TCP fragmentation of ClientHello, or disable TSO/GSO on the appliance. Also verify the appliance does not rewrite SNI or strip ALPN.

maria rodriguez: I filed support ticket SUP-2026-9812 and flagged for escalation to eng/networking if the NGFW vendor doesn't provide a firmware/config fix. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Created ticket <https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-2026-9812> for tenant t-9823.

alex wang: Thanks everyone — will close once the customer confirms NGFW vendor patch or config change. :+1:
